You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Hashcards

A plain text-based spaced repetition system.

Features:
- Store flashcards as plain Markdown files (front/back and cloze cards supported).
- Content-addressable cards: cards are identified by the hash of their text.
- Low friction: edit cards with your editor of choice; use standard tools and VCS.
- Efficient scheduling using an established spaced-repetition algorithm.

Example deck (a Markdown file):

```
Q: How many neurons are there in the human brain?
A: ~80 billion.

C: An [agonist] is a ligand that binds to a receptor and [activates it].
```

Installation

Download a pre-built binary from the project's releases page: https://github.com/eudoxia0/hashcards/releases

Usage

Start a drilling session for a directory containing your Markdown decks:

```
$ hashcards drill [DIRECTORY]
```

Common commands

- drill [DIRECTORY]      Start a drilling session (launches a local web interface).
- stats [DIRECTORY]      Print collection statistics (JSON output supported).
- check [DIRECTORY]      Check integrity of a collection.
- orphans list|delete    Manage orphan cards in a collection.
- export [DIRECTORY]     Export a collection to JSON (prints to stdout by default).

Configuration & data

Runtime data (such as review progress) is stored in a collection database (e.g. an SQLite file) in the root of your card collection directory. This README intentionally omits implementation-specific details (internal schemas, build instructions, and developer notes).

For detailed user-oriented documentation and examples, see the example/ directory (if present) in this repository.

document.addEventListener("keydown", function (event) {
  // Skip during text input.
  if (event.target.tagName === "INPUT" && event.target.type === "text") {
    return;
  }

  const keybindings = {
    " ": "reveal", // Space
    u: "undo",
    1: "forgot",
    2: "hard",
    3: "good",
    4: "easy",
  };

  if (keybindings[event.key]) {
    // Ignore modifiers.
    if (event.shiftKey || event.ctrlKey || event.altKey || event.metaKey) {
      return;
    }
    event.preventDefault();
    const id = keybindings[event.key];
    const node = document.getElementById(id);
    if (node) {
      node.click();
    }
  }
});

EXE="./executable"
def run(name,content):
    base=f"/tmp/front_{name}"; shutil.rmtree(base,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(base); open(base+"/A.md",'w').write(content)

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, builder::PossibleValue};

fn directory_arg() -> Arg {
    Arg::new("directory")
        .value_name("DIRECTORY")
        .help("Path to the collection directory. By default, the current working directory is used")
        .long_help("Path to the collection directory. By default, the current working directory is used")
}

fn cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("hashcards")
        .version("0.3.0")
        .about("A plain text-based spaced repetition system.")
        .subcommand_required(true)
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .subcommand(
            Command::new("drill")
                .about("Drill cards through a web interface")
                .arg(directory_arg())
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("card-limit")
                        .long("card-limit")
                        .value_name("CARD_LIMIT")
                        .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(usize))
                        .help("Maximum number of cards to drill in a session. By default, all cards due today are drilled")
                        .long_help("Maximum number of cards to drill in a session. By default, all cards due today are drilled"),
                )
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("new-card-limit")
                        .long("new-card-limit")
                        .value_name("NEW_CARD_LIMIT")
                        .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(usize))
                        .help("Maximum number of new cards to drill in a session")
                        .long_help("Maximum number of new cards to drill in a session"),
                )
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("host")
                        .long("host")
                        .value_name("HOST")
                        .default_value("127.0.0.1")
                        .help("The host address to bind to. Default is 127.0.0.1")
                        .long_help("The host address to bind to. Default is 127.0.0.1"),
                )
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("port")
                        .long("port")
                        .value_name("PORT")
                        .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u16))
                        .default_value("8000")
                        .help("The port to use for the web server. Default is 8000")
                        .long_help("The port to use for the web server. Default is 8000"),
                )
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("from-deck")
                        .long("from-deck")
                        .value_name("FROM_DECK")
                        .help("Only drill cards from this deck")
                        .long_help("Only drill cards from this deck"),
                )
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("open-browser")
                        .long("open-browser")
                        .value_name("OPEN_BROWSER")
                        .value_parser(clap::builder::BoolValueParser::new())
                        .help("Whether to open the browser automatically. Default is true")
                        .long_help("Whether to open the browser automatically. Default is true"),
                )
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("answer-controls")
                        .long("answer-controls")
                        .value_name("ANSWER_CONTROLS")
                        .value_parser([
                            PossibleValue::new("full").help("Show all four rating buttons (Forgot/Hard/Good/Easy)"),
                            PossibleValue::new("binary").help("Show only two rating buttons (Forgot/Good)"),
                        ])
                        .default_value("full")
                        .help("Which answer controls to show:")
                        .long_help("Which answer controls to show:"),
                )
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("bury-siblings")
                        .long("bury-siblings")
                        .value_name("BURY_SIBLINGS")
                        .value_parser(clap::builder::BoolValueParser::new())
                        .help("Whether or not to bury siblings. Default is true")
                        .long_help("Whether or not to bury siblings. Default is true"),
                ),
        )
        .subcommand(
            Command::new("check")
                .about("Check the integrity of a collection")
                .arg(directory_arg()),
        )
        .subcommand(
            Command::new("stats")
                .about("Print collection statistics")
                .arg(directory_arg())
                .arg(
                    Arg::new("format")
                        .long("format")
                        .value_name("FORMAT")
                        .value_parser([

        .subcommand(

                .subcommand(Command::new("list").about("List the hashes of all orphan cards in the collection").arg(directory_arg()))

        )
        .subcommand(

                        .value_name("OUTPUT")
                        .help("Optional path to the output file. By default, the output is printed to stdout")

                ),
        )
}

}
